line: Did you know, a fatberg heavier than an elephant was pulled from under Cadogan Place?
fact: In 2020 Thames Water found a 10-tonne fatberg of grease, fat and wet wipes under Cadogan Place in Belgravia. They said it weighed more than an African elephant.

line: Did you know, London's first railway tunnel runs under Primrose Hill?
fact: The tunnel under Primrose Hill was London's first railway tunnel, dug for the London and Birmingham Railway in the 1830s. Its entrances have barely changed since.

line: Did you know, Great Turnstile in Holborn is named after a gate for cows?
fact: Great Turnstile is named after turnstiles put up in Tudor times. They stopped cattle grazing in the fields from wandering into Holborn.

line: Did you know, Britain's first heart transplant happened on Westmoreland Street?
fact: In 1968 Donald Ross and his team carried out Britain's first heart transplant on Westmoreland Street, where the National Heart Hospital then stood.

line: Did you know, Monty Python started in a flat on Basil Street?
fact: In the 1960s, the first meetings that led to Monty Python's Flying Circus were held in a flat on Basil Street, Knightsbridge.

line: Did you know, a scientist worked out that time on Church Row ran 10.2 seconds apart from Soho?
fact: The scientist Henry Cavendish had a house on Church Row and another in Soho. He worked out that midday came exactly 10.2 seconds apart at the two.

line: Did you know, there's a swimming pool hanging between two buildings in Nine Elms?
fact: The Sky Pool at Embassy Gardens is a swimming pool that bridges the gap between two blocks of flats, high above the ground. It's see-through, so it looks like a glass box floating in mid-air.

line: Did you know, a hollow oak tree in Greenwich Park was used as a prison?
fact: The hollow trunk of an old oak tree in Greenwich Park was used as a prison. Anyone caught breaking the law in the park was locked inside behind a heavy wooden door.
source: Wikipedia: Queen Elizabeth's Oak, Greenwich Park

line: Did you know, the bells of an Ealing church now ring in a cathedral in Aberdeen?
fact: St Stephen's Church in Ealing was declared unsafe in 1979, and its eight bells were taken down. In 1987 they were restored and hung in St Machar's Cathedral, Aberdeen.

line: Did you know, Becontree station opened with no roads leading to it?
fact: Becontree station opened in 1926, as Gale Street Halt, to serve the new Becontree Estate. At first, no roads led to it.

line: Did you know, Gants Hill station was built after a look at the Moscow Metro?
fact: London's Underground engineers advised on the Moscow Metro in the 1930s. Their report on it led to a station built in London to a similar design: Gants Hill.

line: Did you know, an English army beat an invading Danish army at Brentford in 1016?
fact: In 1016 the English army, led by Edmund Ironside, beat Cnut's invading Danish army at Brentford. The English lost many men, and Cnut beat them in Essex later that year.

line: Did you know, Whitehall Palace had a screen so passers-by couldn't see the king in his bath?
fact: The king's rooms at Whitehall Palace looked over the Privy Garden. A screen stopped people walking past from seeing him naked in his bathtub.
source: Wikipedia: Privy Garden of the Palace of Whitehall

line: Did you know, the band Madness made their name at a Camden pub?
fact: The band Madness first played the Dublin Castle, a Camden pub, in January 1979. The landlord gave them a regular slot, and that's where they made their name.

line: Did you know, a door on Chenies Street leads to a wartime shelter used to plan D-Day?
fact: An entrance on Chenies Street leads down to a deep shelter under Goodge Street station. The US Army Signal Corps used it while preparing for D-Day.

line: Did you know, Kew's Great Pagoda lost its 80 dragons and got them back?
fact: Kew's Great Pagoda had 80 gilded dragons on its ten roofs, all gone by 1784. They're back after the restoration.

line: Did you know, an oak in Southgate is thought to be 800 years old?
fact: The Minchenden Oak in Southgate is thought to be 800 years old, one of the oldest trees in London. It survives from the ancient Forest of Middlesex.

line: Did you know, David Bowie first sang lead at a Blackheath pub, by accident?
fact: In 1963 a 16-year-old David Bowie played sax with the Konrads at the Green Man. The singer cut himself on glass, so Bowie took over.

line: Did you know, London's first trains ran from Bermondsey?
fact: London's first trains ran in February 1836, between Spa Road in Bermondsey and Deptford. The line only reached London Bridge later that year.

line: Did you know, the first sans serif type with lower-case letters was made on Fann Street?
fact: William Thorowgood of the Fann Street Foundry designed the first sans serif type with lower-case letters: plain letters, without the little strokes at their ends. He called it Grotesque.

line: Did you know, the first successful British film was shot outside a house in Barnet?
fact: In March 1895 Birt Acres filmed outside his home, Clovelly Cottage on Park Road, Barnet. Incident at Clovelly Cottage was the first successful motion picture made in Britain.

place: Bull and Mouth, St Martin's le Grand
line: Did you know, the Bull and Mouth Inn was named after a French harbour?
fact: The Bull and Mouth Inn was first called the Boulogne Mouth, after the French harbour Henry VIII besieged in the 1540s.

line: Did you know, the statue of Charles II in Soho Square once stood in a fountain?
fact: The statue of Charles II was once the centrepiece of a fountain in the middle of Soho Square, built in 1681. The fountain was a modest copy of a famous one in Rome.
source: Wikipedia: Statue of Charles II, Soho Square
